items.title: For an affine morphism the pushforward is an equivalence from quasi-coherent modules on the source to quasi-coherent modules over the pushforward algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the module version of the affine equivalence: for an affine morphism f with pushforward algebra A, the pushforward gives an equivalence from quasi-coherent modules on X to quasi-coherent modules over A, and a module over A is quasi-coherent over the base exactly when it is quasi-coherent over A (statement lines 1895-1919). The counted proof constructs the quasi-inverse explicitly as a tensor product over the pulled-back algebra, then produces the unit and counit of the adjunction and reduces their verification to a single algebra identity (proof lines 1922-1965). It is H2: the construction is carried out in full and the argument is not a citation, but the last sentence of the statement is disposed of by the author with a citation to a same-chapter lemma, and the verification of the algebra identity is left to the reader with the author's phrase 'We omit the details'; the counted content is therefore the explicit construction of the equivalence and of its comparison maps.
